title: security: `POST /api/v1/security/explain` with an empty `object` answers `500 EXPLAIN_FAILED`, a malformed request answered as a server fault
body:
domain:server#2 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgUCizoYWQVJWjhdR6F

Found by the contract review of PR #27714 (#27442), record `6507706351` (observation c; read from the code, not measured). Out of that card's scope.

## What is wrong

`ExplainRequestSchema.object` is `z.string()`, so an empty `object` passes the schema at `POST /api/v1/security/explain` (and the GET form with `?object=`). The engine then throws a plain `Error('request.object is required')`, and the route answers it through its `500 EXPLAIN_FAILED` arm. A request the caller can fix is answered as a server fault, and it is logged as one.

Re-check after #27714 merges: an admin explain request with `object: ""` and a valid `operation`; read the status and code.

## Expected

An empty `object` is refused `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` in the route's own envelope, the same as #27714's empty `userId`, before any evaluation. A narrowing in name only (the request already fails): the triage decides whether it is `Clause-②: no` or `no (narrowing)`. Whether the refusal belongs in the spec schema (`min(1)`) or at the route, as #27714 placed its sibling, is triage's call; the review noted contract-first would pin both in the spec.

Filed without `domain:*`; grading is triage's.
